# chartgx

> Inspect matplotlib figures for misleading or broken charts. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes an annotated storyboard.

chartgx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. An agent writes a chart
as a Python file that builds a matplotlib figure; `chartgx inspect` reads the
figure's artist tree, reports every problem, writes a storyboard image with the
problems outlined, and exits non-zero when there is an error.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/chartgx" chartgx --help
uv tool install ./packages/chartgx          # from a clone
```

Needs Python 3.10+, matplotlib, numpy and Pillow.

## Use

```sh
chartgx inspect chart.py            # report + storyboard, exit 1 on any error
chartgx inspect chart.py --json     # machine-readable report
chartgx inspect chart.py --no-storyboard
chartgx render  chart.py -o out.png
```

A chart file defines a figure — a module-level `fig`, a `build()` returning one,
or whatever `matplotlib.pyplot` has open.

## The loop

1. Write the chart as a Python file.
2. `chartgx inspect chart.py`; read the problems (each has a stable `code`).
   A chart declared as data (a figspec model, JSON) is checked without matplotlib
   and without running anything: `chartgx inspect chart.json`. It has no
   storyboard here (a declaration has no artists to box) — the renderer that owns
   the model draws one: `figspec storyboard model.json -o model.storyboard.svg`.
   Unknown keys or unreadable members exit 2.
3. Fix the `error` and `warn` problems; inspect again.
4. Look at `<name>.storyboard.png` — each numbered box proves a problem.
5. `chartgx render chart.py -o chart.png` for the final still.

## Checks

error: `truncated-baseline`, `clipped-text`, `text-overlap`, `log-nonpositive`,
`empty-chart`, `mismatched-lengths`, `non-finite-value`, `two-error-shapes`,
`negative-error`.
warn: `no-title`, `no-xlabel`, `no-ylabel`, `dual-axis`, `too-many-series`,
`pie-slices`, `constant-series`, `clipped-data`, `legend-covers`,
`inverted-axis`.
info: `small-text`, `no-units`, `cut-value-axis`, `red-green`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
